papers.title: Noise Propagation and Effective Channels in Encrypted Quantum Cloning
papers.abstract: We investigate noise propagation in encrypted quantum cloning by formulating the protocol in terms of effective recovery channels. For local single-qubit completely positive trace-preserving noise, a Pauli-basis expansion of the Kraus operators reveals a strong dependence on the location of the physical channel. Noise on an auxiliary signal qubit leaves the reduced recovered state unchanged, whereas noise on an auxiliary key qubit induces a Pauli-diagonal effective channel on the recovered qubit. For the core qubits, the error propagation additionally depends on the parity of the number of entangled pairs. In particular, for noise on the core key qubit with odd parity, distinct physical Pauli sectors merge into the same effective sector, converting isotropic depolarizing noise into an anisotropic recovery channel. We also relate Werner-type resource imperfections to local depolarizing noise and distinguish distributed product depolarization from genuine global depolarization. The results demonstrate that the effective recovery noise is governed not only by noise strength, but also by its physical location and by the structure of the encryption-decryption protocol.
authors: Yun-Fei Li, Fei-Hao Yang, Qing Chen, Liu-Jun Wang

papers.title: Circuit complexity of coupled four-mode squeezed states in two-field inflation
papers.abstract: We study the circuit complexity of coupled curvature and entropy perturbations in two-field inflation. We start from the quadratic action and derive the full Hamiltonian. The Hamiltonian includes all diagonal and off-diagonal quadratic terms. We then obtain three coupled equations for the pair amplitudes of the four-mode squeezed state. From these amplitudes, we calculate the two principal squeezing strengths. We use them to determine the Nielsen circuit complexity. For an equal-weight Gaussian circuit, the complexity takes the form $\mathcal{C}_{2,k}=\sqrt{2(r_{1k}^{2}+r_{2k}^{2})}$. It depends on the squeezing strengths but not explicitly on the squeezing angles. Our numerical results show that the complexity grows after horizon crossing in both coupled and uncoupled models. Interfield coupling changes the pair amplitudes and the four-mode squeezed state. However, its effect on the circuit complexity is small for the parameters considered. This result shows that different four-mode pair-amplitude matrices can yield similar values of the chosen equal-weight circuit complexity. The present calculation provides a reference for studying Gaussian circuit complexity in more general two-field inflationary models.
authors: Tao Li, Hai-Bing Fu, Lei-Hua Liu

papers.title: Active Approach to Fast Quantum State Preparation and Reset in Atomic Arrays
papers.abstract: Rapid preparation of a target quantum state and reset to the many-body ground state are essential for quantum information processing. Here, we investigate both processes in a waveguide-coupled emitter array in the low-excitation regime. By decomposing the effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian into biorthogonal eigenmodes, we show that relaxation depends on the initial overlap with the more subradiant modes, providing a modal explanation of the Mpemba effect. Guided by this insight, we design a reset protocol in which a finite-duration local drive activelysuppresses the relatively slow-decaying components. For the parameters studied, this reduces the time to reach a fixed residual-excitation threshold by up to approximately 25% compared with free decay. To prepare a target Dicke state, we introduce a two-step protocol that initially leaves one emitter undriven before restoring the full drive that stabilizes the target. This local control redistributes spectral weight into the more subradiant modes, driving them closer to their target amplitudes, which reduces the preparation time by up to approximately 45% while consuming less driving energy than continuous driving. Finally, we show how directional waveguide coupling shifts collective modes toward a preferred boundary through the non-Hermitian skin effect, providing guidance for selecting the preferred site for local operations. We term this fundamental dependence of the relaxation dynamics on the system's chirality the ``non-Hermitian Skin-Mpemba effect.'' These results demonstrate how selective local control can accelerate state preparation and reset in open quantum systems.
authors: Ya-Tang Yu, Wei-Hsuan Chung, Tian-Shu Gou, Kuan-Ting Lin, H. H. Jen

papers.title: Hybrid CutFEM-IFEM model for embedded and immersed interfaces with triply-cut cells for the 2D Poisson problem
papers.abstract: We present a hybrid CutFEM--IFEM method for 2D Poisson problems with an immersed fluid--fluid interface and an embedded fluid--solid interface on a single unfitted mesh. The proposed method leverages the strengths of both unfitted finite element methods and immersed interface techniques to handle complex interface geometries and strong discontinuities efficiently. A composite equivalent polynomial representation of the Heaviside and Dirac delta functions is used to integrate on triply-cut cells. Moreover, the IFEM basis functions are enriched with the lift functions exactly representing solution and flux jumps. Numerical examples show optimal convergence for linear and quadratic elements, with accuracy comparable to that of a mesh fitted to both interfaces.
authors: Darsh Nathawani, Christopher Kees

papers.title: Maximally-Matched Mixture Decoding for Correlated Atom Loss in Quantum LDPC Codes
papers.abstract: Heralded atom loss is a dominant noise channel in neutral atom quantum computing platforms, and losses at a two-qubit gate are strongly correlated: when one atom is lost, its gate partner is often lost too. This work shows how to exploit this correlation to construct a better decoder, focusing on [[144,12,12]] Gross code syndrome extraction circuits. Given a loss readout, the possible pairings of the lost qubits according to shared gates form a graph whose maximum matchings carry almost all of the conditional probability mass. Our maximal-matching-mixture (MMM) decoder builds a per-readout decoding hypergraph as a weighted mixture over exactly these loss scenarios. This decoding hypergraph can be used by an ordinary belief-propagation decoder. On the [[144,12,12]] Gross code, MMM lowers the logical error rate by as much as ~25x relative to a loss-unaware decoder and ~2x relative to a loss-aware uniform-mixture baseline from Baranes et al. (2026).
authors: Jacob W. Murri

papers.title: Schur$\unicode{x2013}$Weyl Reduction of Finite-Copy Precision Bounds for Multiparameter Quantum Estimation
papers.abstract: In multiparameter quantum estimation, incompatible measurements can impose trade-offs among estimation errors. Understanding the precision attainable with a finite number of jointly measured copies is therefore important, but direct optimization becomes costly as the tensor product space grows exponentially. For independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) copies, the quantum statistical model is invariant under permutations of the copies. We exploit this symmetry through Schur--Weyl duality to remove permutation multiplicity spaces while using their dimensions as weights. This gives a reduced statistical model equivalent to the original under arbitrary collective measurements. On this reduced model, we derive an exact conic formulation of the tight Cram\'er--Rao bound and a semidefinite program for its Nagaoka--Hayashi (NH) relaxation. For fixed single-copy dimension, the reduced operator representation grows polynomially rather than exponentially with the number of copies. To approximate the tight bound, we use an exact quadratic identity to correct finite-ray dual solutions and obtain rigorous upper and lower bounds. For fixed copy number and parameter dimension, sufficiently fine meshes admit feasible primal points, and dual solutions with bounded objective gaps have uniformly bounded compact-search radii. These results yield quadratic convergence in the projective covering radius. Numerical examples illustrate the quadratic scaling of the mesh correction term and the computational reach of the reduced NH formulation.
authors: Jianchao Zhang, Masahito Hayashi

papers.title: Strict Frequency Bandwidths from Causal Light Cones Enable Scalable Exact Gradient Evaluation in Quantum Optimization
papers.abstract: Dynamical locality is often regarded as a limitation of shallow quantum circuits, yet we show that it can reduce the number of circuit settings required for exact evaluation of gradients with respect to shared parameters. For layered ansatze generated by commuting local terms, strict Heisenberg light cones confine energy slices obtained by varying one shared layer parameter to finite Fourier bandwidths dictated by local causal geometry. This bandlimit recasts exact gradient evaluation as a local signal recovery problem and, when the relevant frequencies lie on a known frequency lattice, yields an exact multipoint parameter-shift rule based on the discrete sine transform. The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) provides a canonical realization in which this mechanism is governed by the local structure of the graph. Specifically, when a cost angle is varied, the relevant geometry is encoded by the contact region in the interaction line graph. At fixed circuit depth on graphs of bounded degree, the number of distinct circuit settings required for the corresponding derivative collapses from $O(m)$ to $O(1)$. This shows that dynamical locality is not merely a constraint on correlation propagation, but also a computational resource that enables exact gradient evaluation with fewer circuit settings in quantum optimization.
authors: Zhaoyang Song, Wei Zhang, Ji Cao, Xuexi Yi, Hong-Fu Wang

papers.title: Time evolution in the multi-component dynamical Keldysh models
papers.abstract: We construct a time evolution operator for a dynamical quantum models with a multi-component random Gaussian field characterized by a long correlation time. We analyze three paradigmatic cases: non-Abelian $SU(2)$ symmetry class for the three-component Gaussian noise and Abelian symmetry classes $U(1)$ and $Z_2$ for the two- and one-component noises correspondingly. Starting with a limiting case of the infinite correlation time (Keldysh model) we shown that statistics of the two-component random field with a non-zero mean is described by the Rice distribution. We derived and solved the system of coupled linear differential equations for the exact diagonal and off-diagonal single-particle Green's functions. We showed how the finite time correlation in Keldysh models are accounted by a continuous fractions method.
authors: M. N. Kiselev

papers.title: Einstein Metrics and Quantum Control on Symmetric Tensor Product Quotients
papers.abstract: Let $M_n=(\mathrm{PU}(2)^n\rtimes S_n)\backslash\mathrm{PU}(2^n)$ be the space of projective $n$-qubit unitaries modulo local unitaries and permutations of the qubits. We prove that for all sufficiently large $n$ the manifold $M_n$ carries exactly two $\mathrm{PU}(2^n)$-invariant Einstein metrics up to scaling. Both Einstein metrics have uniformly bounded diameter after normalizing two-qubit costs, although approximating a Haar-random unitary requires exponentially many two-qubit gates. In contrast, we construct non-Einstein metrics with nonnegative Ricci curvature and exponentially growing typical control distances, and determine the sharp curvature threshold for this family.
authors: Honghuai Fang

papers.title: Symmetry-Preserving Hierarchical Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm with Subproblems Beyond the Qubit Limit
papers.abstract: The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is a paradigmatic variational quantum algorithm for combinatorial optimization problems, yet on current quantum devices the available qubit count and achievable circuit depth remain the main bottlenecks to its practical application. Divide-and-merge reduces the number of variables encoded in a single quantum circuit, while contraction based on coarse graining extends the effective range of shallow circuits, but existing work has not addressed both challenges simultaneously. We propose symmetry-preserving hierarchical QAOA (SP-HQAOA), in which parity sector contraction preserves the zero-field Ising structure of the effective objective at every contraction step, thereby addressing both within a single algorithm. We further prove that this reduction is the unique one with this property. Successive contractions further decouple the maximum leaf block size $B$ from the qubit limit $Q$ per quantum call, so every quantum circuit uses at most $Q$ qubits even when $B>Q$. We also establish a deterministic repair-risk bound on the possible loss in optimal value caused by each sector restriction, and the resulting bounds can be summed across contraction steps and levels of the recursive hierarchy. With depth $p=1$, SP-HQAOA attains $99.4\%$ to $99.7\%$ of the exact optimum on $N=40$ random regular MaxCut leaf blocks and, with at most $10$ qubits per circuit, $96\%$ of the classical reference for $N=500$. SP-HQAOA demonstrates the capacity to use shallow quantum circuits to address combinatorial optimization problems whose variable count far exceeds the qubit limit of a single quantum call, and may enable practical quantum optimization advantages in the near term.
authors: Zhaoyang Song, Wei Zhang, Ji Cao, Xuexi Yi, Hong-Fu Wang

papers.title: Quantum change point metrology
papers.abstract: We quantify the extra Bayes risk of locating a quantum change point and estimating its amplitude with one measurement. The joint and marginal optimizations use the full record and the same joint prior, with both parameters unknown. For product records on a known pure state curve, position has clipped absolute loss in resolution units, and amplitude offset has squared loss in fixed calibrated units. Ideal steps exhibit certified conflict at finite signal strength, including in phase records of sixteen qubits, and recover both informative marginal optima at strong signal. For finite offset prior width, a retained quantum boundary region serves position, and the remaining suffix serves amplitude. Physical recovery holds when strength grows more slowly than the square root of record length. Known smooth rises also admit leading recovery in the coherent experiment as strength grows and width shrinks. For the quintic profile, we establish two residual cost scaling laws. The residual cost is $\Theta(s^{-2})$ as $s\to\infty$. Taking the strong signal limit at fixed $w$ yields a limiting cost of $\Theta(w^3)$ as $w\to0$. In the resolved local model, quadratic position loss admits a common optimum within the covariant class. These results link onset geometry and decision loss to Bayesian measurement compatibility in quantum change point estimation.
authors: Xu Chen, Xue Ma

papers.title: Tachyon and massless sectors of the bosonic string effective action
papers.abstract: Recently, it has been observed that in certain schemes of the bosonic string effective action, the non-derivative tachyon appears only in the tachyon potential, while all other couplings involve covariant derivatives of the tachyon and massless fields. Within these schemes, a minimal basis can be found whose coupling constants are constrained by T-duality upon circle reduction. Using this constraint, one obtains sets of couplings at each order of \(\alpha'\) that are invariant under Buscher rules supplemented by higher-derivative corrections for all base-space fields except the tachyon. In this paper, we observe that consistency of these T-dual sets with S-matrix elements requires an appropriate field redefinition, such that each set becomes invariant under Buscher rules supplemented by higher-derivative corrections for all base-space fields except the metric, dilaton, and tachyon. This separates the couplings into a massless sector and a tachyon sector. We determine the six-derivative couplings in the massless sector, with all coupling constants fixed, and find two T-dual couplings in the tachyon sector with arbitrary coupling constants. We show that the leading-order action and the massless-sector couplings exactly reproduce the expansion of the sphere-level S-matrix element of two tachyons and two massless vertex operators at six-momentum order, and that the coupling constant of the four-tachyon coupling in the tachyon sector is fixed by the expansion of the four-tachyon S-matrix element at six-momentum order.
authors: Mohammad R. Garousi

papers.title: Genericity of singularities of solutions to quasilinear systems on compact sets
papers.abstract: We study the genericity of singularities of types $A_2,A_3,D_4^\pm$ in solutions of the equations of gas dynamics and nonlinear geometrical optics. The sets of solutions satisfying the corresponding transversality conditions are proved to be open and dense in spaces of smooth and real-analytic solutions equipped with the Whitney topology on compact sets.
authors: Azamat Shavlukov

papers.title: Spectral Reduction Selects the Observable Imprint of Dirac Quantum Geometry
papers.abstract: Spectral constraints can alter the observable manifestation of quantum geometry without changing the local eigenspace. Relativistic electron vortices provide a sharp example: the spin orbit interaction redistributes spin and orbital angular momentum, yet its magnetic contribution differs between localized three-dimensional wave packets and stationary monochromatic beams. We resolve this discrepancy by showing that fixing the energy replaces ambient momentum derivatives in position-weighted current moments by shell-tangent derivatives and derive a Hermitian selection rule for first-order observables in momentum-dependent internal subspaces. Its extension-independent form applies beyond Dirac systems, including a broad class of antisymmetric first moments of scalar-charge velocity currents. For the free positive-energy Dirac doublet, the magnetic correction is an exact non-Abelian Berry-curvature contraction with a pointwise saturable quantum-metric bound. Changing the relative phase between the two $\sigma_z$ spinor components switches this correction from zero in a conserved transverse-helicity sector to a finite value in a radial coherent superposition. At fixed finite Lorentz factor, the radial response scales as $O(\theta/\gamma)$, compared with $O(\theta^2)$ for longitudinal polarization. Spectral reduction and internal coherence thus provide distinct controls of the observable imprint of quantum geometry.
authors: Zhongze Guo, Bei Xu, Qiang Gu

papers.title: Fermionic Unruh effect revisited: Entanglement and correlation dynamics under symmetric transformations
papers.abstract: A uniformly accelerated observer perceives the Minkowski vacuum as a thermal bath, so acceleration acts as a noise channel on correlations shared with an inertial partner. For a Dirac field in the standard treatment, the resulting map is a one-sided amplitude-damping channel, and entanglement and quantum discord survive at infinite acceleration. We introduce a symmetric Unruh-like map in which the vacuum and the one-particle state both exchange amplitude with the inaccessible Rindler region; for a Bell state it yields a bit-flip channel whose flip probability is the Fermi-Dirac occupation at the Unruh temperature. Using negativity, mutual information, and all six pairwise quantum discords, we find that the entanglement and discord between the inertial observer and the accessible mode vanish together at infinite acceleration, leaving only one bit of classical correlation. These results show that the fate of quantum correlations in noninertial frames depends on the structure of the Minkowski-Rindler map.
authors: Omid Yahyayi Monem, Hosein Mohammadzadeh

papers.title: Robustness of Magic and the Directed Geometry of State Conversion
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce a state-space distance calibrated by stabilizer states based on the dual structure of the robustness of magic (RoM), and show that RoM is exactly represented as the distance to the free-state set. We then extend this geometry to state conversion by defining the directed conversion deficiency $C_{\mathcal F}$ as the distance between a target state and the set of states freely reachable from a given input state. The quantity $C_{\mathcal F}$ characterizes free convertibility and is related to the minimum stabilizer quasiprobability weight required to represent the conversion residual through the relation $1+2C_{\mathcal F}$. It also contains the conventional magic state resource lower bounds based on RoM and can detect stronger conversion obstructions. For single-qubit systems, we analytically construct a continuous family of mixed states with identical RoM but asymmetric convertibility.
authors: Satoshi Kanno, Yoshi-aki Shimada

papers.title: Controllability-Based Input Allocation in Quantum System
papers.abstract: Understanding how local perturbations influence global quantum dynamics is important for analyzing and designing large-scale quantum systems. Existing quantum centrality measures often rely on static correlations or entanglement and do not directly capture perturbation propagation under unitary evolution. We formulate controllability allocation scoring for quantum input-output dynamics governed by the Schrodinger equation. Using the multiobservable quantum-control Gramian, we introduce virtual local Hamiltonian perturbations along a nominal trajectory and decompose the terminal-output response into channel-wise Gramian contributions. A simplex-constrained log-determinant optimization combines these contributions to define a volumetric controllability allocation score (V-CAS), specifying an optimal allocation of virtual input intensities among local Hamiltonian perturbation directions. The score measures their cooperative dynamical influence and depends on the output and trajectory. We characterize the output Gramian's range and minimum-energy properties and derive a drift-independent sufficient condition ensuring score uniqueness for almost every terminal time at which the problem is feasible. For quantum many-body systems, we develop a matrix-product-state and time-evolving-block-decimation implementation that avoids explicitly constructing exponentially large state-transition matrices. We also derive an error bound propagating Trotter and MPS-truncation errors to the discrete output Gramian. Numerical experiments show that the score captures finite-time influence patterns distinct from those identified by static correlation- and entanglement-based measures and can inform target-independent control-channel preselection.
authors: Riku Yaegashi, Kazuhiro Sato, Kentaro Ohki

papers.title: Gauge-parameter cancellation and finite form factors in one-loop quark scattering in the refined Gribov-Zwanziger framework
papers.abstract: We calculate the one-loop amplitude for distinct-flavor massless quark scattering in a local BRST-invariant refined Gribov-Zwanziger theory with minimally coupled quarks. The constraint determinant and two dynamical quark flavors are included in the action and in the loop sum. Retaining the refined Gribov-Zwanziger masses in the free field matrix, we combine the mixed self-energy insertion, complete vertex and box corrections, and external-leg residues. The difference between a general linear covariant gauge and a reference gauge vanishes symbolically after removal of the Stueckelberg regulator in the specified dimensional prescription. We separate ultraviolet and infrared poles, retaining contributions hidden by scaleless integrals and by the order of mass and dimensional limits. Local modified-minimal-subtraction counterterms close the ultraviolet poles, and the remaining infrared poles cancel in the stated nonzero-mass domain. The finite answer is supplied as eight color-spin form factors over a thirty-entry scalar integral inventory, with all 144 finite-function coefficients provided electronically. The result defines a partonic amplitude on a specified analytic branch; it does not assume colored asymptotic states or establish an inclusive next-to-leading-order cross section.
authors: Wan Wu

papers.title: Finite-volume and thermodynamic-limit lower bounds for the coherently driven Bose--Hubbard model via the Lieb--Yamazaki method
papers.abstract: We derive rigorous lower bounds on the ground-state energy of the coherently driven Bose--Hubbard model using a Lieb--Yamazaki positive-operator decomposition. The resulting quadratic bounding Hamiltonian is diagonalized by displacement and Bogoliubov transformations, yielding explicit stability conditions and finite-volume bounds in arbitrary dimension. We establish the thermodynamic-limit energy density and characterize the excitation spectrum of the bounding Hamiltonian. We also derive its Gaussian-state observables, including filling, number fluctuations, and second-order correlations, and identify regimes of antibunching and sub-Poissonian statistics. Numerical calculations assess the tightness of the bounds across representative parameter regimes.
authors: Maciej Janowicz, Joanna Kaleta, Filip Krzy\.zewski, Andrzej Zembrzuski

papers.title: Hot and dense QCD equation of state from the complex Langevin equation
papers.abstract: We discuss the QCD equation of state at temperatures above the crossover and for high baryon chemical potentials, obtained via the first ever complex Langevin simulations at the physical pion mass. In particular, we present continuum-extrapolated results for the energy, entropy, and enthalpy densities, as well as for the specific heat capacity as a function of baryon chemical potential and temperature.
authors: Michael Mandl, D\'enes Sexty, Daniel Unterhuber

papers.title: The Topological String on the Quintic to Genus 83 and the Rank-Two D4-D2-D0 Indices
papers.abstract: We compute quintic Gopakumar-Vafa invariants for genera 2-83 and degrees up to 44 by integrating the holomorphic anomaly equations. Under rank-one modularity for the required Gieseker invariants and rank-two charge conjugation, a coupled system of boundary and surplus wall-crossing equations fixes the holomorphic ambiguities and 22 of the 36 polar rank-two D4-D2-D0 coefficients, without assuming any rank-two index. A computer-assisted extension of wall crossing supplies additional equations and the boundary datum needed to close the recursion through genus 83. With known low-genus input, the GV data are complete through degree 32 and yield PT and DT tables. Selected higher-genus wall-crossing invariants reach genus 216; 33 entries require additional hypotheses. Retrospectively selected extrapolations give conditional candidates at genera 84 and 85 and, with rank-two mock modularity, for the remaining polar coefficients.
authors: Michael Hecht

papers.title: Coherent Electronic Lensing in Proximitized Graphene
papers.abstract: Spatially resolved control of coherent electron transport offers a route to understanding and engineering interference phenomena in hybrid superconducting devices. Here, we use Scanning Gate Microscopy (SGM) to investigate Fabry-P\'erot (FP) interference in the n-p-n cavity of a ballistic graphene Josephson junction. Spatial maps of the superconducting switching current and normal-state conductance reveal circular interference fringes arising from two distinct effects of the SGM tip potential. A global shift of the Fermi wave vector modulates the FP resonances of the cavity, while a local perturbation produces additional oscillations that persist at fixed Fermi wave vector as the tip bias is varied. An analytical model identifies the origin of this local response with coherent electron lensing, in which the tip modifies the phase accumulated along interfering trajectories. The measured fringe patterns in the switching current indicate that this mechanism affects superconducting transport, consistent with tip-induced shifts of the resonance conditions for Andreev bound states. These results establish SGM as a tunable local lens for controlling interference in superconducting ballistic graphene devices.
authors: Ivan Villani, Samuele Fracassi, Niccol\`o Traverso Ziani, Maura Sassetti, Matteo Carrega, Vaidotas Mi\v{s}eikis, Camilla Coletti, Fabio Beltram, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Sergio Pezzini, Stefan Heun

papers.title: Far Tails of the Positional Distribution in random walk: A Saddle-Point Approach
papers.abstract: Rare events and large-deviation theory have attracted considerable interest in the study of random walks. Here, we investigate the rare events of the positional distribution of continuous-time random walks under ordinary and equilibrium initial conditions using the saddle point method. We show that the far-tail behavior is sensitive to the expansion of the waiting-time distribution near its minimum value. For a general power-series expansion near the minimum waiting time, the positional distribution exhibits an approximately exponential decay in its far tails. In contrast, when the waiting-time distribution has a cutoff at its minimum value, the positional distribution exhibits an unexpected Gaussian decay, in contrast to the far-tail behavior of the renewal-count distribution. We further find that the most likely number of renewals required to reach a given position, as well as the associated rate functions, is insensitive to the initial conditions, whereas the far tails of the positional distribution retain a dependence on the initial conditions. Our results provide new insights into the rare-event statistics and large deviations of random walks.
authors: Chen Zhou, YuDa Cheng, Yangji Li, Jing Xu, Wanli Wang

papers.title: Electromagnetic Potentials via the Extended Maxwell System
papers.abstract: We construct electromagnetic potentials on arbitrary open 3-dimensional sets for anisotropic, non-homogeneous materials, thus rendering any topological assumption like simple connectedness or the absence of holes superfluous in this context. The main idea is to invoke the extended Maxwell system the easy solution theory of which then yields existence of both scalar- and vector potentials.
authors: Rainer Picard, Sascha Trostorff, Marcus Waurick

papers.title: Tan's Contact for Trapped Spin-Orbit-Coupled Fermi Gases at Finite Temperature
papers.abstract: Tan's contact, bridging microscopic features of many-body quantum systems to two-body contact interactions, is pivotal in the description of quantum gases. However, past studies of Tan's contact of the spin-orbit coupled Fermi gases have been exclusively discussed at zero temperature. The thermal effects on that, which cannot be neglected in most experimental conditions, has not been explored so far. Here, through a path integral Monte Carlo (PIMC) study, we show that thermal effects fundamentally alter the scaling relation between spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and Tan's contact. The linear scaling of Tan's contact with respect to the strength of SOC found at zero temperature is drastically undermined by the thermal effects. And a new mechanism based on the competition between the mean occupancy and the energy-reweighted occupancy of the opposite spin fermion pairs within the interaction range has been unveiled, which radically changes the above linear scaling to a non-monotonic dependence. Our work should be useful for future experiments to explore the preternatural thermal effects on Tan's contact of the strongly interacting spin-orbit-coupled Fermi gas.
authors: Tianhao Wu, Yuanbang Wei, Rui Tian, Dongdong Pu, Beizhi Chen, Qihang Ying, Hongyan Shi, Yue Zhang, Shuai Li, Bo Liu

papers.title: Harnessing Non-Markovian Memory for Quantum-Battery Capacity
papers.abstract: Non-Markovianity is commonly characterized through information-theoretic signatures of memory. Here we take a thermodynamic perspective and ask whether such memory can be operationally harnessed to enhance quantum-battery capacity. Within the process-tensor framework, we compare memoryless and memory-enhanced strategies and define their performance gap as the memory-assisted capacity advantage of a multitime process. We prove that this advantage vanishes for Markovian process tensors and is bounded by a trace-distance measure of process non-Markovianity. In a complementary continuous-time setting, we show using random telegraph dephasing that memory accumulated during the evolution can enhance capacity retention relative to a matched Markovian reference under the same control class. These results identify non-Markovian memory as an operational resource for quantum-battery capacity.
authors: Jun-Li Jiang, Xin-Zhu Liu, Xiu-Yong Ding, Xue Yang, Ming-Xing Luo

papers.title: Coherent errors, syndrome extraction and the Robustness of Magic in stabiliser codes
papers.abstract: Coherent errors leave stabiliser-code-encoded magic states in superpositions of syndrome sectors. We ask how much magic these coherent errors add, and whether syndrome extraction depletes logical magic. Using Robustness of Magic, we show that, for a unitary error U on a correctable region which supports no stabiliser, the encoded state has the same robustness as the logical state plus one copy of the Choi state of U , in every stabiliser code encoding. Syndrome extraction removes this copy, returning the logical robustness. The removed magic is positive for every non-Clifford error: adding a non-stabiliser state to any state multiplies one plus the robustness by a (tightly- bounded) factor above one. The magic capacity of two-qubit gates Clifford-equivalent to diagonal or single-qubit gates is equal to their Choi-state robustness. We give a linear-algebraic test for when a Clifford error makes syndrome extraction measure a logical operator, and give magic lifetimes of stored single-qubit magic states under Pauli noise. Choosing the plane of the stored state extends these lifetimes about 1.5x on rotated surface codes under low code-capacity depolarising noise. We identify states and channels in odd-prime dimension for which Wigner negativity and robustness show equal lifetimes.
authors: Enrico Bozzetto, Jonte R. Hance

papers.title: Nonlinear response and retarded three-point correlators of charge transport
papers.abstract: We study nonlinear response of charge transport in relativistic kinetic theory within the relaxation time approximation. For a classical gas of massless charged particles coupled to an external $U(1)$ gauge field, we organize the Boltzmann equation perturbatively in the source and derive a recursive solution for the distribution function to arbitrary response order. At second order we analytically obtain fully retarded three-point correlators at generic frequencies and momenta, verify the Ward identities implied by charge conservation. We also discuss the general properties of these correlators, including their analytic structure, consistency limits, and relation to Schwinger--Keldysh effective theories of diffusive fluctuations.
authors: Jin Hu

papers.title: Learning Grover mixers for constrained optimization
papers.abstract: Grover-Mixer QAOA (GM-QAOA) is a promising quantum framework for constrained combinatorial optimization. However, its practical implementation requires the efficient preparation of a uniform superposition over feasible states. In this work, we propose a two-stage variational approach. First, a parameterized quantum circuit is trained to prepare this superposition, using an entropy-based cost function that favors a uniform distribution over feasible bitstrings. The trained circuit is then embedded in GM-QAOA, where it provides both the initial state and, together with its inverse, yields the Grover mixer. The resulting method is evaluated on two representative benchmark problems: the Maximum Weight Independent Set (MWIS) problem and the Multidimensional Knapsack Problem (MKP). While the results demonstrate consistent improvements over standard QAOA for MWIS, only marginal gains are observed for MKP, with the advantage diminishing as the problem size increases. The reduced performance on MKP reflects the growing difficulty of training the variational mixer, likely due to increasingly challenging optimization landscapes. Overall, these findings highlight both the potential of variational Grover mixers and the trade-off between their performance gains and the additional resources required for their training.
authors: Matteo Vandelli, Francesco Ferrari, Daniele Dragoni

papers.title: Resurgence and Modularity in the First Painlev\'e Equation
papers.abstract: For the first Painlev\'e equation, we relate three nonlinear Stokes maps associated with a full turn around infinity to modular transformations of the two-parameter tau function through the identity $\boldsymbol S_\pi\circ\boldsymbol S_0\circ \boldsymbol S_{-\pi}=\mathsf S\circ\mathsf T$. Here the subscripts label Borel directions, while $\mathsf S$ and $\mathsf T$ denote the modular generators. Working under the analytic assumptions of the topological recursion and exact WKB constructions, we compare Stokes multipliers of the associated isomonodromy system while tracking the homology basis of its elliptic spectral curve under rotations of the independent variable. For the sectors considered, we identify the known parameter transformation induced by an $8\pi/5$ rotation with the modular $T$-action and derive a new explicit parameter relation realizing the $S$-action for a $2\pi/5$ rotation. We also determine the multiplicative factors in the corresponding tau-function relations, including their normalization constants. Together, these results give an explicit realization of single-valuedness after one full turn around infinity for both the Painlev\'e transcendent and its tau function, with the tau-function prefactors cancelling by Abel's five-term identity for the Rogers dilogarithm.
authors: Kohei Iwaki, Noam Tamarin

papers.title: Swimming versus Screening: How Activity Reshapes the Ionic Cloud of a Charged Particle
papers.abstract: A major question in active matter is how interactions between particles are modified by activity. Here, we address this question for Coulomb interactions by considering a charged swimmer immersed in an electrolyte. A static charge is screened by an ionic cloud that decays over the Debye length $\lambda_D$. We show that the persistent motion of the swimmer can qualitatively modify the steady-state ionic charge-density profile. At low activity, the swimmer appears effectively quasistatic to the ions, and conventional Debye-H\"uckel screening is recovered. At higher activity, the ballistic-to-diffusive dynamics of the swimmer are reflected in distinct spatial regimes. A power-law decay is followed by a stretched-exponential decay at intermediate distances. At sufficiently large distances, exponential screening is restored, but with an increased screening length, $\lambda>\lambda_D$, revealing activity-induced underscreening. Thus, active motion modifies both the spatial form and the range of electrostatic screening. Our results motivate the study of active electrolytes composed of positively and negatively charged swimmers.
authors: Tanmoy Chakraborty, Tomer Markovich, Ram M. Adar

papers.title: Pulse-Informed Physical Placement for Parallel Two-Qubit Gates in Qubit Arrays
papers.abstract: A parallel two-qubit layer can often be realized with several nonoverlapping sets of physical couplers, but isolated calibrations do not reveal how each realization performs after optimizing its own simultaneous control pulse. We formulate physical placement and pulse synthesis as a coupled decision problem for parallel controlled-$Z$ gates in heterogeneous frequency tunable transmon arrays. The proposed processor-aware structural quantum multi-domain matrix (QMDM) links static processor, edge, incidence, and task information to a dynamic candidate response block. For each candidate placement $P$, QMDM instantiates the active Hamiltonian $H_P$; quantum optimal control (QOCT) generates a placement-specific pulse, direct coupled propagation returns the projected computational subspace overlap $F_{\rm proj}$ and computational survival; and these pulse-conditioned responses are fed back to QMDM to rank and progressively promote physical placements. This placement pulse response feedback defines pulse-informed physical placement. Here, to see the performance of the proposed method on 30 held-out synthetic $3\times3$ processors, the median final $F_{\rm proj}$ is $0.993826$ for pulse-informed placement and $0.984981$ for calibration-based placement. Also, when tested under different system conditions, the proposed pulse-informed approach uses $59.1\%$ fewer candidate QOCT optimizer iterations than the exhaustive finite-budget reference. The QMDM representation and outer search are formulated for arbitrary $L$ simultaneous two-qubit gates. Here, the present global candidate ranking validation is used for $L=2$.
authors: Shahid Qamar, Wei-Feng Zhuang, Bilal Riaz, Peng Qian

papers.title: The Non-Relativistic Limit of Five-Dimensional Boson Stars and Scale Invariance Violation
papers.abstract: We investigate the non-relativistic limit of spherically symmetric boson stars in (4+1)-dimensional general relativity (GR). In this limit, the resulting Newtonian theory exhibits an exact scale invariance, leading to a critical boson star configuration with a fixed global U(1) charge and vanishing binding energy. We identify the origin of these properties in the restored scale symmetry and analyze how relativistic and gravitational corrections break this symmetry. By comparing the full (4+1)-dimensional Einstein-Klein-Gordon system with the Wick-Cutkosky model, we quantify the effects of these corrections on the energy-charge relation and the kinematic stability of the configurations. Our results demonstrate how weak violation of scale invariance lifts the degeneracy of the non-relativistic solutions and determines the behavior of boson stars away from the critical limit.
authors: Eduard Kim, Oleg Kondrashov, Emin Nugaev, Yakov Shnir

papers.title: Conformal Spectrum of (Super) Chiral Ising and XY Models
papers.abstract: We determine the spectrum of scaling dimensions of composite operators in the critical Gross-Neveu-Yukawa and Nambu-Jona-Lasinio-Yukawa models through a next-to-leading order semiclassical computation. Their infrared fixed points belong to the chiral Ising and chiral XY universality classes, respectively. At next-to-leading order, we resolve the Lorentz structure of the operator spectrum. For the parameter values at which supersymmetry is expected to emerge in the infrared, we obtain a closed-form expression encoding the full spectrum within the semiclassical methodology. The resulting organization of operators into superconformal multiplets provides further evidence for emergent superconformal dynamics.
authors: Oleg Antipin, Jahmall Bersini, Jacob Hafjall, Giulia Muco, Francesco Sannino

papers.title: Two-loop BRST-restoring finite counter-terms for chiral non-abelian gauge theories
papers.abstract: We study the renormalization of anomaly-free chiral $SU(N)$ gauge theories without scalar fields through two-loop order. We adopt the Breitenlohner--Maison--'t Hooft--Veltman (BMHV) scheme for the treatment of $\gamma_5$ in dimensional regularization. This prescription induces spurious breaking of BRST symmetry, requiring finite symmetry-restoring counter-terms in addition to the subtraction of ultraviolet divergences. We derive these counter-terms for a general, possibly reducible fermion representation, thus restoring the BRST symmetry, through two loops.
authors: Achilleas Lazopoulos, Vera Paroutiadou

papers.title: Competition and cancellation in a tilted Rice--Mele chain: exact Wannier--Stark offset and spectral readout
papers.abstract: In a tilted Rice--Mele chain, the Wannier--Stark (WS) ladder becomes staggered, \(E_n=n\Fo+(-1)^{n+1}A\). The offset \(A\) reflects the competition between the staggered onsite energy \(\Delta\) and the dimerized hopping \(\dt\), and its cancellation restores spectral equidistance. We determine \(A\) through a systematic strong-field series in the WS basis and a nonperturbative two-band Floquet expression. An exact matrix element reduces the strong-field expansion to Bessel algebra; at the representative working point, truncation at seventh order locates the cancellation point with a theory-internal truncation error of \(0.010\)~Hz, against \(27.3\)~Hz at first order. The Floquet propagator gives the closed form \(A=(\Fo/\pi)\arcsin(-i\,\mathrm{Tr}\,U/2)\), exact within the two-band model, implying the kinematic bound \(|A|\le\Fo/2\) and identifying cancellation with maximum spectral uniformity. The same analytic structure yields a family of real zeros and complex exceptional points that set the convergence radius of the strong-field series without touching the real axis. On odd-length chains, the hidden-symmetry defect produces a pairing plateau of height \(2|A|\) that persists numerically beyond first order in the modulations, allowing the offset to be read from the static spectrum without Floquet propagation or time evolution. In the bulk, cancellation appears as the merging of two sidebands into a single line at \(\Fo\), a null measurement that requires no calibrated sideband amplitudes, although the tilt and line frequency still need calibration. These signatures provide complementary spectral tests of the staggered WS ladder and a calibration-aware route to precision force sensing.
authors: Xiang Gao, Xing Deng, Shoulong Chen, Ying Zhang, Chunhua Zhang, Wei Xiao, Xueting Fang

papers.title: Quantum Gate Engineering in Superconducting NISQ Platforms: Experimental Methods and Emerging Directions
papers.abstract: This review aims to provide researchers, experimentalists, and quantum engineers with an updated and technically grounded perspective on the implementation of quantum gates in superconducting NISQ devices. The goal is to establish a comprehensive bridge between theoretical quantum circuit synthesis and its practical, experimental implementation, focusing on superconducting quantum technologies. We systematically examine the diverse landscape of superconducting qubits and processor architectures, ranging from conventional transmons to alternative and unconventional designs, evaluating their unique design trade-offs, connectivity constraints, device physics, and materials impact. Moving from theory to actual implementation, we detail how single- and two-qubit operations are synthesized via microwave-driven and flux-activated pulses. We here present our pulse engineering, wave shaping, calibration workflows, demonstrating how to bridge the gap between abstract gate models and real-world hardware limitations in the direction of a hardware-software co-design framework. To validate these operations, we choose benchmarking methodologies with the purpose to get the more efficient metric for the specific evaluation aspect, including truth tables and quantum process tomography. Therefore, we both discuss the theoretical concepts behind the gate synthesis and show experimental implementation of most fundamental gates by proposing a practical workflow.
authors: Alessandro Sarno (Dipartimento di Fisica 'Ettore Pancini', Universit\`a degli Studi di Napoli 'Federico II', Via Cinthia, 80126, Napoli, IT), Viviana Stasino (Dipartimento di Fisica 'Ettore Pancini', Universit\`a degli Studi di Napoli 'Federico II', Via Cinthia, 80126, Napoli, IT), Antonio Pio Italiano (Dipartimento di Fisica 'Ettore Pancini', Universit\`a degli Studi di Napoli 'Federico II', Via Cinthia, 80126, Napoli, IT), Alessandra Pizza (Dipartimento di Fisica 'Ettore Pancini', Universit\`a degli Studi di Napoli 'Federico II', Via Cinthia, 80126, Napoli, IT), Carlo Cosenza (Dipartimento di Fisica 'Ettore Pancini', Universit\`a degli Studi di Napoli 'Federico II', Via Cinthia, 80126, Napoli, IT), Wladislav Guarino (Dipartimento di Fisica 'Ettore Pancini', Universit\`a degli Studi di Napoli 'Federico II', Via Cinthia, 80126, Napoli, IT), Domenico Montemurro (Dipartimento di Fisica 'Ettore Pancini', Universit\`a degli Studi di Napoli 'Federico II', Via Cinthia, 80126, Napoli, IT), Francesco Tafuri (Dipartimento di Fisica 'Ettore Pancini', Universit\`a degli Studi di Napoli 'Federico II', Via Cinthia, 80126, Napoli, IT), Davide Massarotti (Dipartimento di Ingegneria Elettrica e delle Tecnologie dell'Informazione, Universit\`a degli Studi di Napoli Federico II, Via Claudio 21, 80125, Napoli, IT), Halima Giovanna Ahmad (Dipartimento di Fisica 'Ettore Pancini', Universit\`a degli Studi di Napoli 'Federico II', Via Cinthia, 80126, Napoli, IT)

papers.title: Hyperentanglement-enabled Quantum Privacy Amplification for Classical-Quantum Coexistence in Fiber Networks
papers.abstract: Integrating quantum communication into existing fiber infrastructures requires coexisting with high-power classical traffic, which generates noise in the quantum channel. Spontaneous Raman Scattering (SpRS) is the dominant noise source, generating a broadband photon background that degrades quantum states and, in Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), can entirely suppress secure key generation. In this work, we implement single-copy entanglement distillation utilizing energy-time and frequency hyperentanglement, and we exploit it to perform Quantum Privacy Amplification (QPA) directly at a physical layer. Strict frequency anti-correlations of spontaneous parametric down-conversion are used to selectively discard uncorrelated Raman photons while preserving genuine entangled pairs, suppressing accidental coincidences by a factor $1/N$, where $N$ is the number of frequency channel pairs. Using passive borosilicate-glass photonic integrated circuits and standard DWDM demultiplexers over a 20~km single-mode fiber testbed, we demonstrate a 4~dB improvement in tolerance to classical laser launch power $P_C$ when QPA is performed, extending the secure key threshold from $P_C=-13.3$ dBm to $P_C=-9.3$ dBm. The result shows that off-the-shelf telecom components can be repurposed as physical-layer quantum privacy amplifiers.
authors: Domenico Ribezzo, Giulia Guarda, Alessandro Zavatta, Davide Bacco

papers.title: Inhomogeneous Geometric Last Passage Percolation and the $q$-deformed Jacobi Unitary Ensemble
papers.abstract: We study directed last passage percolation with geometric weights in a spatially inhomogeneous environment. We derive an explicit limit shape and establish fluctuation limits for the passage time, showing that, depending on the strength of the inhomogeneity, the limiting fluctuations are governed by Fredholm determinants associated with either the Airy or Bessel kernel. Our approach is based on an exact relation between the passage time and the smallest particle of the $q$-deformed Jacobi unitary ensemble ($q$-JUE). As part of our analysis, we derive the macroscopic limiting density of the $q$-JUE, which provides a natural $q$-deformation of the classical Wachter distribution, as well as of the limiting distribution of the Meixner ensemble. We further establish Airy and Bessel scaling limits for the smallest particle, which are of independent interest.
authors: Sung-Soo Byun, Yeong-Gwang Jung, Nick Simm

papers.title: Information-Theoretic Reliability--Safety Bounds and Finite-Alignment Dynamics in AI Knowledge Distillation
papers.abstract: The reliability and safety of artificial intelligence (AI), together with their transfer and evolution through knowledge distillation, have attracted growing attention. We establish an information-theoretic bound on the reliability--safety trade-off and characterize the dynamics of this trade-off under knowledge distillation. We first prove a universal trade-off inequality that is independent of the specific model form. Its boundary is determined solely by a single parameter Kh, which quantifies the hidden layer's ability to distinguish benign from hazardous inputs. We then develop a canonical Boltzmann-machine model of AI response behavior and derive two exact relations between reliability and safety. The trade-off curve is determined by the hazard discrimination capacity K, while the overall answer tendency controls the operating point along the curve. These relations agree well with existing experimental data. In knowledge distillation, we find that teacher responses induce a renormalization of the student model's trade-off parameters. We further use a renormalization-group approach to study multigenerational distillation, deriving exact recursion relations and the associated renormalization-group-like flows for two representative direct intergenerational distillation protocols at arbitrary teacher--student alignment strength. These flows reveal fixed-point structures, long-term dynamics, and critical behavior, yielding testable predictions for the critical transition between capability loss and stable transmission.
authors: Miao-Miao Yi, Zhen-Yu Cai, Y -M. Du, C. P. Sun

papers.title: Finite-time minimum-work protocols for underdamped traps driven by active forces
papers.abstract: Active systems provide non-equilibrium energy that can, in principle, be harvested using control protocols, making the optimization and reliability of work extraction a fundamental problem in microscopic thermodynamics. Yet how inertia and activity jointly modify the optimal work extraction protocol, the maximum extractable work its fluctuations, and implementability of protocols remains unclear. Here, we design minimum-work protocols, which maximize work extraction whenever extraction is possible, for an underdamped active particle in a translated harmonic trap. Remarkably, both the minimum mean work and its fluctuations are independent of mass, although inertia modifies the protocol. The results are then applied to an underdamped active Ornstein-Uhlenbeck particle (AOUP), designing an explicit work-extraction criterion and revealing extracted work's dependence on rotational noise and initial conditions. We further show that inertia strongly affects the difficulty of implementing the optimal protocol, producing a transition-like change between underdamped and overdamped optimal protocols. These findings uncover work extraction mechanisms at the microscale and guide the design of reliable energy-harvesting microscopic devices and robots.
authors: Kangcan Yao, Ruicheng Bao, Zhonghuai Hou

papers.title: Probing micron-range fifth forces with cold atoms in optical tweezer arrays
papers.abstract: We propose a new method to search for fifth forces at micron scales, by resonantly exciting the motional state of ground-state-cooled atoms in optical tweezer arrays. We develop a homodyne readout protocol based on sideband thermometry, which can approach the Standard Quantum Limit, and expand the discovery reach for fifth forces by up to four orders of magnitude compared to existing constraints. We show that this level of sensitivity can also probe well-motivated models of extra dimensions beyond the current tabletop state of the art, by leveraging the parametric enhancement of higher-dimensional gravity.
authors: Marios Galanis, Andrew A. Geraci

papers.title: Bootstrapping Wilson lines in Critical Bosonic QED$_3$ Part 1: Large-$N$ endpoint correlators and CFT data
papers.abstract: We study the conformal Wilson line with general charge $q$ in critical bosonic QED$_3$ with $N$ complex scalar flavors by combining diagrammatic four-point calculations with endpoint crossing. We formulate the endpoint crossing equations with the full $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ flavor structure, keeping positivity manifest. For arbitrary positive integer charge $q$ held fixed at large $N$, we obtain closed-form expressions for four-endpoint correlators and mixed correlators involving two bulk Hubbard--Stratonovich fields through first subleading order in $1/N$. These results determine the endpoint dimension, the defect $g$-function, and the dimensions and endpoint OPE coefficients of the lowest non-singlet Wilson-line primaries. Moreover, combining the diagrammatic correlator with endpoint crossing, somewhat surprisingly, we find agreement between the bulk and Wilson-line spectra in every non-singlet flavor channel through order $1/N$. At degenerate levels, this agreement concerns the OPE-weighted averages of anomalous dimensions probed by the endpoint correlator. For unit charge, we independently reproduce these averages from the known bulk higher-spin spectrum.
authors: Jun Maeda, Toshiki Onagi, Soichiro Shimamori

papers.title: Homodyne versus heterodyne detection for classifying families of optical quantum states from finite records of detection events
papers.abstract: Neural networks can identify an optical quantum state from an image of its phase-space function, but a real measurement gives a finite record of $N$ detection events. Heterodyne detection samples the Husimi $Q$ function directly, whereas homodyne detection gives the Wigner function only after a reconstruction from several phases. We ask which scheme better identifies one of seven families of states, including Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states, under loss, dephasing and Gaussian noise. We simulate finite records on identical states for two sets of families, one with equal mean photon number and one built from the code of Ahmed et al. For convolutional networks, heterodyne detection outperforms homodyne detection with filtered back-projection by 14.1 percentage points at $N=100$ events and 20% dephasing in the first set (adjusted $p=0.003$ over $24$ cells across training runs), and it depends on the number of phases and on the reconstruction. At $N=10^3$ and $10^4$ no difference is significant, but the intervals are wide. At $N=100$, a homodyne network without reconstruction does not differ significantly from heterodyne detection in the first set and is nominally worse in the second. Near thermal states we show to leading order that heterodyne detection damps phase-space structure of order $n$ exponentially, whereas homodyne detection shares unit weight among $n+1$ angular components, a local result that does not explain the finite-record differences. Experimental records of a GKP state, photon-subtracted squeezed states and one mode of an Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen source are classified like simulated ones, but these low-power tests probe our counting-noise model, not the seven-class accuracy. A likelihood-ratio observer shows no such gap at $N=100$, so our evidence concerns a reconstruction-based pipeline, not homodyne detection in general.
authors: Franciszek Grzywa, Sebastian Dolata, Karol Bartkiewicz

papers.title: Goldbach Representations in Quantum Optics and Metrology
papers.abstract: We derive a relation between Goldbach representations and photon-number statistics in a quantum-optical setup. Considering an even-number Fock state injected into a stochastic beam splitter with uniformly distributed transmissivity and projections of the two output modes onto prime subspaces, we demonstrate that each successful outcome corresponds to an Goldbach representation and that the averaged detection probability is exactly proportional to the number of Goldbach representations. Then, employing the Hardy--Littlewood asymptotic formula, we demonstrate that the post-measurement state generated by a beam splitter with fixed transmissivity exhibits standard quantum limit scaling of the ultimate precision limit in terms of phase estimation, whereas an equally weighted superposition of Goldbach representations exhibits Heisenberg scaling. These results provide a quantum-optical realization of Goldbach representations and relate their statistics of with quantum metrology.
authors: Akira Sone, Maxim Olshanii

papers.title: Topological interfaces between universes and generalized families of 2d QFTs
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional quantum field theories with topological point operators decompose into universes. Just as fusion categories have played an important role in understanding non-invertible symmetries, multi-fusion categories play an analogous role for the symmetries of such decomposing theories. We describe a finite symmetry as a multi-fusion category together with its action functor, which keeps track of trivially acting symmetries and of the topological interfaces between universes. Relative to a chosen symmetry, we classify pairs of universes by the topological interfaces it contains, which reflect the structure of the multi-fusion category: universes in different indecomposable summands are joined by no interface (Type~III), while within a summand they are related by invertible (Type~I) or only non-invertible (Type~II) interfaces. For orbifolds with a trivially acting abelian normal subgroup, we derive the full inherited symmetry, which characterizes the operators between universes found case by case by Robbins, Sharpe and Vandermeulen and yields pairs of Types~I and~II but never of Type~III. We construct Type~III pairs instead from extensions of $2$-group type and from renormalization group flows out of a common ultraviolet theory. Finally, we propose a correspondence with the generalized families of quantum field theories of Brennan and Intriligator, in which equivariant families correspond to Type~I pairs and categorical ones to Type~II pairs whose gauging preserves the symmetry, family anomalies appear as universes carrying different symmetry-protected topological phases, and Type~III pairs can realize families over a discrete parameter. An appendix by Xingyang Yu works out the higher-charge Schwinger model as a Lagrangian example.
authors: Pinak Banerjee, Yuhan Gai, Alonso Perez-Lona, Daniel Robbins, Subham Roy, Eric Sharpe, with an appendix by Xingyang Yu

papers.title: Quantum Observables of Nonperturbative Superradiant Scattering
papers.abstract: Inelastic scattering from $N$ coherent spins, or any two-state system, scales as $N^2$, invalidating the Born approximation at large $N$ even at weak coupling. We develop a nonperturbative theory of this superradiant scattering and its backreaction on the spins. Since one particle can exchange many quanta, the target's energy-transfer and energy-variance rates keep their favorable $N^2$ scaling even after the cross section saturates, unless a conservation law limits each encounter to exchange of one quantum. We apply the theory to millicharged-particle searches, as well as neutron and charged-particle beams that can test quantum protocols for detecting cosmic relics.
authors: Asimina Arvanitaki, Savas Dimopoulos, Marios Galanis, Derek J. Li

papers.title: Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization for Variable Molecular Geometries
papers.abstract: Quantum and hybrid quantum-classical algorithms have the potential to improve the accuracy and scale of quantum chemistry and impact a broad range of applications such as drug discovery and catalysis. In particular, subspace methods such as sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) can already tackle classically challenging systems. However, practical algorithms that go beyond the computation of electronic ground and excited states are still scarce. Here, we introduce the variable-geometry sample-based quantum diagonalization (VGSQD) algorithm, which extends SQD to variable molecular geometries by reusing quantum samples from a reference geometry at displaced ones, thus significantly reducing quantum computational cost. Using circuits of up to 124 qubits on ibm-quebec, an IBM Heron r2 quantum processor, we determine the equilibrium geometry and energy of the weakly bound, strongly correlated beryllium dimer, as well as the water molecule. Finally, we extend VGSQD to chemical reactions and compute the minimum energy path and energy barrier of a hydrogen exchange reaction. The results are comparable with state-of-the-art classical methods such as CCSD(T) and DMRG. This work broadens the scope of quantum algorithms for chemistry, from energies to geometry optimization and reaction pathways, both essential for practical applications.
authors: Matthieu Fortin-Deschenes, Ibrahim Shehzad

papers.title: The Effective Field Theory Origin of the Fuzzy Sphere Method
papers.abstract: Fuzzy sphere Hamiltonians for (2+1)D conformal field theories are usually written directly on the lowest Landau level. We introduce a framework organizing them as descendants of local ``mother theories'' on $S^2\times\mathbb R$. We start with the example of Ising mother theory built from two charged Dirac fermions coupled to a real mediator $\phi$. Integrating out $\phi$ and the higher Landau levels produces the fuzzy Hamiltonian, while integrating out the fermions gives a conventional local $\phi$ effective field theory flowing to the Ising point. Mild modifications of the same theory reach the Gaussian point (tricritical route) and the Lee-Yang continuation. Exploring the space of mother theories, we next promote $\phi$ to a complex field $\Phi$ and construct a new example, whose descendant is an easy-plane ferromagnet on the fuzzy sphere. Its spontaneous symmetry breaking phase gives a pseudo-Goldstone relativistic scalar, similar to the model introduced by Y.-C. He, while its critical point is non-relativistic, providing the first example of $z=2$ scaling on the fuzzy sphere. Remarkably, it admits exact one-magnon solutions, and the $z=2$ critical point can be found analytically. We then outline a rich landscape of further applications of our approach.
authors: Mykola Dedushenko

papers.title: Gravitational anomaly spectroscopy of a Kitaev spin liquid
papers.abstract: The chiral central charge $c$ measures the gravitational anomaly of a two-dimensional topological phase. It fixes the heat current carried along the edge. So far, it has been accessed through thermal transport, where phonons complicate the signal, or through wave-function probes that need a pure ground state. Here we show that $c$ is a spectroscopic quantity of the edge. A weak modulation of the edge couplings that travel along the edge is absorbed according to the Virasoro algebra. Normalized by the response to a static change of the same couplings, the absorbed weights obey $D_n=2n\langle L_0\rangle+\frac{c}{12}(n^3-n)$, so that $\mathcal{C}\equiv2D_2-4D_1=c$ in any state of the ideal edge theory, thermal or not. The central charge thus appears in transition weights, although it cancels from excitation gaps. The ratio of line weights with and without a vison in the bulk, $\Lambda=4h_\sigma/c$, needs no calibration and fixes the conformal spin $h_\sigma$ of the non-Abelian Ising anyon. For the Kitaev honeycomb spin liquid we find $\mathcal{C}=0.49999$ and $h_\sigma=0.06250$ on 7168 spins. Calibrating with the shift of the measured line itself gives $c$ within about $1\%$ on 96 spins and within $1\%$ under $20\%$ random coupling errors. Interacting edge Majoranas in a fixed flux sector, treated with DMRG, keep $\mathcal{C}$ within $1.5\%$ while the edge velocity changes by $\pm13\%$. An exact simulation of a quantum-processor protocol, including the native Floquet circuit, returns $c$ within $3.5\%$ on 96 to 600 spins.
authors: Kumar Ghosh

papers.title: Quenched Thermodynamics from Ancilla-Assisted Imaginary-Time Evolution
papers.abstract: Quenched thermodynamics combines the equilibrium physics of fixed coupling configurations with a prescribed distribution of disorder. Problems related to quenched thermodynamics are generally intractable to approximate. We provide a quantum algorithm to calculate quenched disorder averages for the transverse-field Ising model, whose coupling configurations are organized into gauge classes. We show how to estimate these averages by preparing approximate Gibbs states through ancilla-assisted imaginary-time evolution. At each measurement, the ancilla record identifies the gauge class to which the energy estimate contributes. We validate our framework through an open $3\times3$ lattice. A one-step circuit resolves all sixteen flux classes, and a finite-shot calculation estimates the quenched energy for independently distributed bond signs. Thermodynamic integration extends the reconstruction to a quenched free-energy estimate, while comparison with exact diagonalization identifies the finite-step approximation as the dominant source of error. This use of the measurement record provides access to the thermodynamics of frustrated spin systems with a disorder distribution chosen independently of the circuit's sampling frequencies.
authors: Ibukunoluwa Adisa, Daniele Cuomo

papers.title: Unifying energy-entropy bounds in semiclassical gravity
papers.abstract: We revisit bounds on energy and entropy in semiclassical gravity, aiming to strengthen and unify established bounds, in particular the quantum focussing conjecture (QFC) and the smeared null energy condition (SNEC). Both the QFC and SNEC have important applications and are the strongest in their respective hierarchies; however, neither implies the other, nor reduces to the null energy condition (NEC) in the classical limit. To that end, we define a new class of bounds dubbed gravitational energy-entropy conditions (GEECs) that imply both the QFC and SNEC, and reduce to the NEC classically. We construct an explicit family of GEECs by imposing the defining criteria on a broad set of stress tensor bounds, and constrain its remaining parameter space through test cases, in an effective field theory-inspired approach. Our GEECs are powerful candidate bounds on energy and entropy in semiclassical gravity.
authors: Jackson R. Fliss, Andrew Rolph

papers.title: Collective Bootstrap for Matrix Quantum Mechanics
papers.abstract: We develop a collective bootstrap framework for large $N$ matrix quantum mechanics formulated directly in the loop space of single trace coordinate moments. Loop joining and splitting operations organize the kinetic constraints systematically and avoid treating momentum containing moments as independent variables. Employing the virial theorem, a Schur complement, and a relaxation of quadratic products of loops, we recast the nonlinear constrained optimization of the collective energy into a semidefinite program, which yields a lower bound on the planar ground state energy at every truncation. A sequential semidefinite optimization heuristic then searches for configurations satisfying planar factorization and estimates the ground state energy and loop expectation values. Applications to one-, two-, and three-matrix models exhibit close agreement with analytic solutions and master field optimization. By working exclusively with coordinate moments, the framework permits truncations at higher word length and offers a promising approach to models with more matrices, including the bosonic sectors of the BFSS and BMN models.
authors: Xianlong Liu

papers.title: A Primer on Instanton Physics - A Short Course
papers.abstract: These six lectures, delivered at the University of New Brunswick 6-21 October 2026, are an introduction to instantons in quantum mechanics and quantum field theory for senior undergraduate and beginning graduate students. The first four lectures deal solely with particle mechanics, building the necessary background for the last two that cover applications in semi-classical field theory.
authors: Pervez Hoodbhoy

papers.title: Large connectivity expansion of Ising Spin Glasses on random graphs
papers.abstract: We compute a high-connectivity analytical expansion for Ising spin glasses on sparse random graphs. We expand the cavity equations around the fully-connected mean-field limit, focusing on the critical behavior of the system: our approach allows us to compute the de Almeida-Thouless line of mean-field finitely-connected systems in the temperature $T$--magnetic field $H$ plane, by means of closed analytical equations. The exact cavity solution of such systems can only be obtained by solving numerically iterative equations, so our approach brings a notable computational advantage. On the theoretical side, we are able to identify three sources of corrections to the fully-connected mean-field solution: i) the non-Gaussianity of the cavity fields, ii) the statistical correlation between the cavity fields and their fluctuations, and iii) the corrections to the cavity filter functions. These corrections are treated using two different expansions: a non-uniform expansion, where we expand all three contributions around the mean-field solution, and a uniform expansion, where we only expand the statistics but leave the cavity filters untouched. The former allows for a direct comparison with the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model but fails at low temperatures, as a consequence of the de Almeida-Thouless line diverging in the zero-temperature limit. On the other hand, the uniform expansion describes with good accuracy the critical behavior of the system. We also extend these results to the $T = 0$ limit.
authors: Luca Maria Del Bono, Flavio Nicoletti, Federico Ricci-Tersenghi

papers.title: Elliptic master integrals and the one-loop cosmological wavefunction
papers.abstract: Loop corrections to the cosmological wavefunction involve similar integrals to those required for scattering amplitudes. For the one-loop triangle of a conformally coupled scalar, the master integrals are elliptic, and so the triangle wavefunction coefficient was expected to be elliptic as well. Using a bootstrap approach, we compute this triangle coefficient exactly and show that it is not: the elliptic periods cancel, and the flat-space wavefunction coefficient is a combination of dilogarithms. The cancellation occurs because the residue of the loop integrand on the elliptic sector is a flat-space amplitude, rational in the loop momentum. The one-loop box, by contrast, is not polylogarithmic, even with a single external leg at each site. Its threshold discontinuity involves elliptic integrals, which we also give in closed form. For regular-tetrahedron momenta the periods of a K3 surface enter its loop integrand.
authors: Amara McCune, Matthew D. Schwartz

papers.title: Mixed-State Topological Transition and Emergent Fractionalized Supersymmetry in the Non-Abelian Kitaev Spin Liquid
papers.abstract: We study a mixed-state topological transition in the non-Abelian Kitaev spin liquid driven by a bond-dephasing channel. In the vectorized picture, bond dephasing maps onto interactions between two time-reversed fractionalized Majorana systems coupled to gapped $\mathbb Z_2$ gauge fields, enabling sign-problem-free Monte Carlo simulations. We show that increasing dephasing condenses an inter-copy fermion pair, converting ${\rm Ising}\boxtimes\overline{\rm{Ising}}$ to toric-code order in the Choi state and yielding intrinsically mixed-state topological order upon unfolding. More interestingly, at a temporal interface between topological and trivial Kitaev states, a Chern-number mismatch enforces a gapless Majorana mode. Dephasing then drives a mixed-state topological transition at which the gapless mode develops emergent $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetry. Our Monte Carlo simulations yield $\nu=1.27(3)$ and $\eta_b\simeq\eta_f\simeq0.40$, consistent with the exact supersymmetric values $5/4$ and $2/5$. The supersymmetric partners are fractionalized and appear physically as distinct gauge-invariant spin strings, providing concrete observables for future experiments.
authors: Zhou-Quan Wan, Hong Yao, Shao-Kai Jian

papers.title: Searching for Dark Photons and ALPs using Gamma-rays from Nuclear Reactors
papers.abstract: Nuclear reactors are intense sources of MeV gamma rays, produced in fission, radiative neutron capture and the de-excitation of fission products. Building on earlier phenomenological studies, we present a detector-independent description of the production of light, weakly coupled particles by reactor gamma rays and of their detection through scattering, absorption and decay in a nearby detector. We consider kinetically mixed dark photons, produced and detected through Compton-like processes, and axion-like particles (ALPs) coupled to photons, electrons and nucleons, produced through Primakoff conversion, Compton-like scattering and magnetic nuclear transitions such as the $2.23~\mathrm{MeV}$ line of $p(n,\gamma)d$. As a concrete application, we derive the projected sensitivities of the CONUS+ germanium experiment at the Leibstadt reactor and of a conceivable $100$-kg CONUS100 upgrade. For sub-MeV dark photons, CONUS+ and CONUS100 reach kinetic mixings of $\epsilon\simeq1.65\times10^{-5}$ and $1.2\times10^{-5}$, respectively, for $0.5~\mathrm{keV}\lesssim m_{A'}\lesssim0.5~\mathrm{MeV}$. For ALPs, we show that CONUS100 can probe an unexplored region of parameter space at MeV masses, in particular through $a\to e^+e^-$ decays of ALPs emitted in the deuteron line, assuming a energy window extended to $10~\mathrm{MeV}$.
authors: Lucia Angel, Manfred Lindner, Farinaldo S. Queiroz, Bilge S. Solak

papers.title: Predicting $B^{(*)}\bar D{}^{(*)}$ states from a reanalysis of lattice QCD data
papers.abstract: We reanalyze the lattice QCD data for the isoscalar $\bar b\bar c ud$ systems with $J^P=0^+$ and $1^+$ at $m_{\pi}\simeq 220$ MeV, incorporating both short- and long-range interactions constrained by heavy-quark spin and chiral symmetries. Using the interaction fitted to the lattice results, we predict a spectrum of isoscalar $B^{(*)}\bar D{}^{(*)}$ molecular states with quantum numbers $J^P=0^+$, $1^+$, and $2^+$. The predicted $J^P=0^+$ and $1^+$ $B\bar D$ and $B^*\bar D$ bound states are consistent with the lattice results. Furthermore, the two resonances reported by the lattice collaboration in the $J^P=0^+$ and $1^+$ $\bar b\bar c ud$ channels can be naturally interpreted as $B^*\bar D{}^*$ and $B\bar D{}^*$ hadronic molecules, respectively. We also predict two previously unreported $B^*\bar D{}^*$ states with $J^P=1^+$ and $2^+$: a bound state and a shallow state whose pole may correspond to either a virtual state or a bound state, respectively. Our results provide a unified interpretation of the lattice spectrum and highlight the interplay between short- and long-range interactions in the dynamics of the $B^{(*)}\bar D{}^{(*)}$ systems.
authors: Pan-Pan Shi, Miguel Albaladejo, Meng-Lin Du, Feng-Kun Guo, Victor Montesinos, Juan Nieves

papers.title: From pq-webs to magnetic quivers and back I: dictionary and deformations
papers.abstract: This is the first of two companion papers in which we study five-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ theories engineered by $(p,q)$ five-brane webs and their associated three-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=4$ magnetic quivers. We focus on the $N+\mathrm{SU}(N)_0^{k-1}+N$ box quiver theories. We propose an exact parameter dictionary relating the five-dimensional flavour masses and instanton couplings to the Fayet-Iliopoulos parameters of the corresponding strong-coupling magnetic quiver. We test this dictionary through a broad class of deformations, including mass deformations, weak-coupling limits, and vacuum expectation values. On the five-dimensional side, we implement these flows directly at the level of the superconformal index. The dictionary fixes the corresponding FI deformations and monopole VEVs. We analyse them in the magnetic-quiver squashed-sphere partition function using a new method that tracks Higgsing, decoupled sectors, and infrared theories. Our results promote magnetic quivers to tools for the quantitative study of how the five-dimensional superconformal index responds to deformations.
